newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek telecom invests billions in foreign deals.
newsitem.headline: Greek telecom invests billions in foreign deals.

text.p: Greek telecom company OTE will invest 100 billion drachmas ($423.3 million) in joint ventures abroad in the next four years, company officials told a news conference on Wednesday.

"We expect an eight percent yield until the year 2000 from this investment. Doing business abroad is something relatively new for OTE but it is absolutely necessary to operate in the tough telecommunications environment," the head of international relations for the Hellenic Telecommunications Organisation (OTE) Vassilis Maglaras said.

He said OTE would invest mainly in Balkan, eastern European and Middle East countries in areas like mobile telephony, construction of land and submarine lines and buying stocks of privatised telephone companies.
OTE has already signed a deal for installing 49,000 digital lines in Lithuania and building a 570-kms fiber optics network.
It is part of an international consortium biding for developing a GSM mobile network in Romania and wants to buy a major stake in the Armenian state telecoms company Armentel.
It also plans projects in Georgia, Bulgaria, Albania, and the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.
OTE will see a pretax earnings growth of 17.8 percent in 1996 with pretax profit expected to reach 240 billion drachmas from 203.7 billion in 1995, officials told Reuters.
Based on its IPO prospectus, the telecom had projected pretax earnings of 259 billion drachmas this year, equity analysts said.

Sales in 1996 will grow 26.4 percent to 750 billion drachmas from 593 billion a year earlier. They will exceed a projected 700 billion drachmas in the IPO prospectus. --Costas Paris, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 236.2 Greek Drachmas)
